proposal.rationale:
## Verdict
Proceed with the supplied configuration. I found no parameter that is clearly inappropriate for this run, so I am not recommending a change. This is a plan review only. No analysis has run, no results exist yet, and no literature was retrieved, so I cite nothing.

## Question
Do expression-only clusters of Visium spots in this single adult mouse brain section form spatially coherent groups on the hexagonal lattice? Which candidate genes show spatial autocorrelation (Moran I) and differ across clusters (descriptive Kruskal-Wallis H)? Clusters are not checked against any reference labels, so anatomical identity is not assumed.

## Inputs
- Filtered 10x feature-barcode matrix (H5) from the V1 adult mouse brain dataset.
- Spot coordinates are used only for lattice adjacency and downstream spatial statistics. They do not enter clustering.

## Methods
1. Library-size normalization to 10,000 counts, then log transform.
2. Keep genes detected in at least 3 spots.
3. Select 2,000 HVGs by expression dispersion alone.
4. Scale with a maximum value of 10, then run PCA with 30 components.
5. Build a 15-neighbor expression graph, then run Leiden and UMAP. UMAP is for display only.
6. Test same-cluster agreement on immediate hexagonal neighbors against fixed-size label shuffles.
7. Compute Moran I and Kruskal-Wallis H for the same 200 expression-selected candidate genes.

## Parameters
- Seed 42.
- Leiden resolutions 0.3, 0.5 and 0.8.
- 999 randomizations.
- Mirrors the sensible defaults for this data type. The 3-spot gene filter is permissive and may keep sparse genes, which is acceptable because candidate ranking and spatial statistics are reported descriptively.

## Review stops
- QC is chosen only after QC plots are reviewed. Expected checks include total counts, detected genes and mitochondrial fraction per spot, to test whether clusters track technical quality.
- The primary resolution is chosen only from expression diagnostics (cluster stability and size distribution) before any tissue map is viewed.
- This plan requires review before execution. Any change to the configuration needs a new run.

## Null hypotheses
- Edge agreement: cluster labels are spatially unrelated to the lattice. Observed same-cluster neighbor agreement should match the fixed-size shuffled-label distribution.
- Moran I: a gene has no spatial autocorrelation. With 999 permutations, the smallest attainable p-value is about 0.001.
- Kruskal-Wallis H: a gene's expression distribution is the same across clusters. Results are descriptive ranks, not significance tests.

## Independent checks
None is available in this run. Cluster-derived DE and spatial statistics computed on the same clusters are not independent confirmation. No reference labels, external datasets or retrieved sources exist to test the clusters against. Any external check would need an explicit new input.

## Limitations
- Single section, so no replication across animals or sections.
- Quality confounding is possible, so clusters may reflect depth or mitochondrial content rather than biology.
- Isolated spots and small clusters may be unstable. Mixed spots at boundaries are expected in Visium.
- Only immediate hexagonal neighbors are used, so larger-scale structure is not captured.
- Resolution sensitivity is reported across 0.3, 0.5 and 0.8 rather than assumed away.
- Testing 200 genes across three resolutions creates multiplicity. Results will be descriptive and need adjustment or caution.
- Gene-function and anatomical interpretations remain unverified evidence gaps until supported by retrieved sources.

Observed: 2702 in-tissue spots, 32285 genes, 13 mitochondrial genes, no zero-count spots. Quantiles: total_counts 1%=8188, 5%=12130, 50%=28944, 95%=60817, 99%=84329, max=156413. n_genes_by_counts 1%=2405, 5%=3358, 50%=6019, 99%=9324, max=10934. pct_counts_mt 50%=15.3, 95%=23.6, 99%=28.0, max=43.2. The histograms are unimodal with right-skewed counts and mt. The counts-versus-genes scatter is tightly coupled along one curve. Low-depth outliers (about 580 to 4500 counts) sit below the bulk and include several high-mt points. Only a handful of spots sit above 100000 counts or 10000 genes.

Decision: inclusive thresholds that trim only the extreme tails, since the user asked for inclusive retention. min_counts=5000 removes only the sparse low-depth tail below the 1% quantile (about 8 visible points under 5000). min_genes=2000 is below the 1% quantile (2405) and removes only the lowest-complexity spots. max_counts=100000 and max_genes=10000 sit above the 99th percentiles, so they remove only the top outliers while keeping high-density tissue. max_pct_mt=30 sits just above the 99th percentile (28.0) and removes the high-mt tail.

Tissue quality gradients: the spatial maps show that the high-count and high-gene spots form broad regions rather than random noise. Mitochondrial fraction is elevated along the left edge and in a curved band, and some low-count spots carry high mt. These patterns may reflect tissue quality, cell-type composition, or section-edge effects. QC here cannot separate these causes, so retained high-mt spots in those regions should be checked in later diagnostics rather than assumed to be damaged.

Alignment: the overlay plots show the spot grid within the section outline and metric values confined to the tissue area. This supports visual alignment of spots to the imaged section only. I did not identify any anatomical structure, and I make no anatomical claims. Alignment accuracy at fine scale remains uncertain.

Limits: single section, no independent replicate, and thresholds are distribution-based rather than validated against biology. Literature retrieval was not used for this step, so no external support is claimed.

proposal.reason: Resolution 0.5 gives 14 clusters with sizes from 29 to 338 spots; the sizes sum to 2668, matching the filtered spot count. Resolution 0.3 gives 10 clusters (minimum 56) and resolution 0.8 gives 16 clusters (minimum 56). ARI is 0.787 between 0.3 and 0.5, and 0.732 between 0.3 and 0.8. The 0.3-to-0.5 overlaps are nearly nested: most 0.3 clusters map mainly to one or two 0.5 clusters, with small leakage. The PCA variance ratio falls from 10.1% on PC1 to about 2.0% on PC30, with no sharp elbow in the supplied table, so the configured 30 PCs were kept. In the expression UMAPs, the 0.5 partition separates compact islands that appear as broader groups at 0.3, while retaining the main 0.3 structure. Inference: 0.5 is the most defensible of the three computed options, adding granularity without the larger ARI drop seen at 0.8; it also matches the proposed baseline. Caveats: 0.5 cluster 13 has only 29 spots and sits as an isolated tail, so it may be a small-group or mixed-spot artifact. The 0.8 partition is not ruled out. Stability rests on one seed and one parameter set, and ARI between neighboring resolutions is not a formal stability test. No tissue map was supplied, so no spatial or anatomical claims are made. The QC rationale mentions spatial maps not in the supplied evidence, so those statements are unverified. No retrieved literature supports this choice.

feedback: External reviewer feedback (Claude Code, claude-opus-5-5, 2026-10-29); attribute reviewer-computed numbers to the reviewer, not to the pipeline. Revise DRAFT.md: (1) Resolution ordering is verifiable: api/003 contained only the three UMAP images; cluster approval was logged at 22:39:04 UTC and the tissue cluster map was written at 22:39:09 UTC. Remove the claim that ordering cannot be confirmed. (2) qc_tissue.png was supplied with the QC request; remove the T1 caveat that the QC review spatial statements are unverified. (3) PC30 variance is 0.0020 (0.20%), not 2.0%. (4) Address technical confounding at the cluster level (reviewer-computed): pct_counts_mt Kruskal-Wallis H = 983 across the 0.5 clusters and total_counts H = 748, which would rank about 35th and 66th among the 200 candidates; Moran I is 0.55 for pct_counts_mt and 0.45 for total_counts. Cluster 13 (median 66059 counts, 9.1% mt) forms a thin continuous arc on tissue that coincides with the high-count arc in qc_tissue.png; describe this as observation, not anatomy. Also report that partitions into 14 quantile groups of total_counts or pct_counts_mt give edge agreement of only 0.14 and 0.17, versus 0.78 observed. (5) For T4, explain what each statistic measures: H is between-cluster separation of expression distributions, Moran I is similarity between lattice neighbours. Use Dnali1, 2900040C04Rik and Pmch with gene_cluster_means.csv to show why each one has discordant ranks. (6) Gm4952 is detected in 0.4% of spots; describe its bottom rank as a sparsity effect, and note 10 candidates are detected in under 1% of spots. (7) State explicitly that the global label shuffle shows labels are not randomly placed but cannot separate organisation beyond smooth expression variation. (8) Remove the reference to an undefined weak_both category. Keep observed, inferred and external claims separate; do not add anatomy without retrieved sources.

review.reviewer: The user (human), 2026-10-29. The user reviewed the plan, QC, resolution choice and analysis outputs, sent one feedback round and accepted revision 1. The user later confirmed reading and agreeing with revision 1 and visually checked the tissue overlay against H&E.
review.independent_check: Independent checks reviewed by the user (separate from the run verifier): rebuilt the hexagonal lattice from array_row/array_col (2668 spots, 7679 edges, degree 1-6, 0 isolates); joined all 2668 barcodes to raw datasets/visium_mouse_brain/spatial/tissue_positions_list.csv with 0 coordinate mismatches; recomputed edge agreement 0.780049 (0.5), 0.825759 (0.3), 0.78057 (0.8); empirical tail (1+0)/1000 = 0.001 with saved null max 0.1017; own 999-shuffle null (seed 7) mean 0.088 SD 0.0032; confirmed quoted gene values in gene_rankings.csv; confirmed resolution chosen before tissue maps (api/003 had 3 UMAP images; approval 22:39:04 UTC, tissue map written 22:39:09 UTC). All matched. Also computed QC covariates on the same graph: pct_counts_mt H=983, total_counts H=748, Moran 0.55/0.45; 14 quantile groups of counts/mt give edge agreement 0.14/0.17.
review.agent_weakness: Draft 0 errors: claimed resolution ordering could not be confirmed (refuted by logs); repeated the false caveat that QC tissue maps were not supplied (qc_tissue.png was in api/002); PC30 variance 2.0% vs actual 0.20%; did not test whether clusters track QC metrics despite planning to; described Gm4952 (detected in 0.4% of spots) as near-uniform rather than sparse; thin DE-vs-Moran explanation. Most were corrected in revision 1 after the user's feedback; the residuals below were documented for correction. Residual in accepted text: 2900040C04Rik H written as 400 (table 431.9, error introduced in revision); maps line still calls Gm4952 near-uniformly low. Reviewer error: feedback asked Haiku to use gene_cluster_means.csv, which is not in the report packet, so discordant-gene mechanisms remain labelled hypotheses.
review.uncertainties: Whether coherence reflects genuine domains or smooth expression/technical gradients (global shuffle does not preserve autocorrelation; QC-quantile benchmark argues against depth/mt alone but does not settle it); identity of cluster 13 (thin high-count arc) and the stable 56-spot group; per-cluster basis of discordant genes; no external sources retrieved, so no biological or anatomical claims; the user visually checked alignment against H&E; this does not establish anatomical identities; single section, seed and parameter set.

changes: Corrected reviewer attribution, accepted status, the H value, sparse gene wording, cluster size and discordant-gene discussion. Added reproduced cluster means and clarified the internal-edge denominator. The draft retains its historical scientific content; only its reviewer attribution and historical-draft notice changed.
